headline: Path-integral, graph, and fitness-landscape models of clonal selection dynamics
label: Clonal Fitness Landscape Modeling
summary: Quantitative models of clonal selection now infer treatment optima, drug response contextuality, and karyotype fitness from longitudinal and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is mathematical modeling of selection acting on evolving populations, with fitness or response parameters inferred from time-resolved data. The antibody affinity-maturation study uses a stochastic model calibrated to in vivo lineage and deep mutational scanning data, and applies a path-integral method to identify optimal antigen-dosing schedules. The AML framework uses an edge-weighted digraph to represent how cytarabine response depends on cellular context, and extends to SAMHD1 inhibitor exploration with a web-based implementation. ALFA-K infers chromosome-level karyotype fitness landscapes from longitudinal single-cell data and predicts emergent aneuploid karyotypes. What is new is the shift from describing clonal composition to inferring the fitness landscapes that govern it and using them to prescribe interventions.
